AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Amputation of a lower-limb results in a severe decrease of functional mobility that deeply alters independent living. Motor imagery (MI) refers to the mental representation of an action without engaging its actual execution. The repetitive use of MI has been shown to contribute to promote motor recovery and phantom-limb pain alleviation.

AbstractText.Label: AIM
AbstractText.content: Given the importance of invoking accurate images to benefit from MI practice, and considering the link between motor capacities and MI, the present study investigated the effect of a rehabilitation program on MI ability in patients with lower-limb amputation.

AbstractText.Label: POPULATION
AbstractText.content: Patients with trans-tibial or trans-femoral amputation, following a rehabilitation program as outpatients.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: MI ability of the patients was measured at three different time point along the course of physical therapy.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The data revealed i) a positive effect of the rehabilitation program on MI accuracy of locomotor tasks, and ii) greater MI vividness and accuracy for single-joint movements that patients were still able to physically perform.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: These findings suggest that MI abilities and actual motor performance are mirrored in a congruent fashion.

AbstractText.Label: CLINICAL REHABILITATION IMPACT
AbstractText.content: Therapists should consider this critical aspect when including MI practice in rehabilitation programs among patients with lower-limb amputation.
